subject: general
question: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Both Q and V are immediate neighbours of S. V sits third to the left of T. R sits to the immediate left of T. U is not an immediate neighbour of V. How many people sit between S and U when counted from the right of S?
solution:
**Given:** P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) Both Q and V are immediate neighbours of S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/000e74901a53683913456606dcdc8925a4fee6739953a6d6cd1fee8027e27d9d.png] 

2) V sits third to the left of T.

3) R sits to the immediate left of T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f79e5c358e0bec72cf9ac37a3339dd97f88f67f156f0ef45198fa2cea3084aa1.png] 

4) U is not an immediate neighbour of V.

After positioning U only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. P.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3a91c990372ff0e7694a2396637895341bffe7bcf76fbabd809583f652a370c.png] 

Thus, four people sit between S and U when counted from the right of S.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.
